etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French intermittent, from Latin intermittens (“sending between”), from prefix inter- (“among, on”) + mittens (“sending”), from mittere (“to send”).
senses: Stopping and starting, occurring, or presenting at intervals; coming after a particular time span.
(specifically, geology, of a body of water) Existing only for certain seasons; that is, being dry for part of the year.
(medicine, dated) An intermittent fever or disease.
